answer: Oak staves stand in a ring by the churn-maker bench, bound with iron hoops. Proof of churn-maker via butter churn tally — a churn the churn-maker staves only after 271 churns hold true without one leaking at the stave, each staved by the churn-maker himself. umber fits the dasher through the lid and tests the wobble. inlet planes each stave true and drives the hoops down tight. raven fills the churn with cream and works the dasher till the butter comes. Two hundred and seventy-one churns must hold true without one leaking at the stave, and the next still leaks where the oak ran green.
